title: How do we get half the area of a quadrilateral?
description: A grandmother wants a flower bed with half the area of her four sided garden. The video joins the midpoints of the four sides, shows each corner triangle is a quarter of a diagonal triangle, and finds the four corners make up exactly half.
teaching_notes: One idea: each corner triangle is a quarter of a triangle made by a diagonal, so the four corners are half of the shape and the inner quadrilateral is the other half. Watch for students who think a diagonal always halves the shape.

source: Figure it Out (area of any polygon, question 5)
video_script.why: The child applies the split by a diagonal into two triangles method of the solved example, and uses half the base and half the height to get a quarter.
video_script.substitution: Join the midpoints of the sides in order, then compare each corner triangle with a triangle made by a diagonal.
video_script.anchor: a grandmother's uneven four sided garden ABCD with the midpoints P, Q, R, S of its sides joined in order
video_script.payoff_line: Join the midpoints in order and the inner quadrilateral has half the area

final_answer.value: Join the midpoints of the sides in order; the inner quadrilateral has half the area
final_answer.spoken: join the midpoints in order and the inner quadrilateral has half the area

video_script.fraction_reading: half and quarter are said as words
hold_back: Join the midpoints of the sides in order; the inner quadrilateral has half the area
never_show: a diagonal shown splitting an uneven quadrilateral into equal halves
the answer before the answer beat
maths_rules: quadrilateral ABCD; P, Q, R, S are the midpoints of AB, BC, CD, DA
corner triangle APS has AP = 1/2 AB and AS = 1/2 AD at the same corner A, so its area is 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4 of triangle ABD
likewise triangle CQR = 1/4 of triangle CBD; so APS + CQR = 1/4 (ABD + CBD) = 1/4 of ABCD
with the diagonal AC: triangle BPQ = 1/4 of triangle BAC and triangle DRS = 1/4 of triangle DAC; so BPQ + DRS = 1/4 of ABCD
four corners = 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2 of ABCD; inner PQRS = 1 − 1/2 = 1/2 of ABCD
check on a 6 by 4 rectangle (area 24): the midpoints make a shape with a diagonal of 6, and two triangles on it each have height 2: 2 × (1/2 × 6 × 2) = 12 = 24 ÷ 2
video_script.design: One idea: corners are quarters of diagonal triangles. One uneven quadrilateral stays as the anchor all video. The check uses a 6 by 4 rectangle.
